title: New neighbors
scene: A family of immigrants moves into Anna's building. They talk about their green card, the consulate and the consul, about racism and a racist neighbor, about the poor ghetto where they lived and their hope to join the middle class; Grandpa, born in the baby boom, is a baby boomer and a nationalist, and they argue about nationalism.

words.ex: I came to Poland as an immigrant in 2022.
She finally got her green card after five years.
She went to the consulate to get a visa.
The consul helped the lost tourists.
Racism is still a problem in many countries.
He was fired for being a racist.
He grew up in a poor ghetto.
I grew up in a family from the middle class.
There was a baby boom after the war.
My father is a baby boomer, born in 1955.
He is known as a strong nationalist.
Nationalism grew stronger after the war.
Many migrants crossed the border last year.
My grandpa is a boomer, born in 1955.
Many millennials work from home now.

old_story: A family of [[immigrants|immigrant]] moved into Anna's building last week. Their son lives in America and just got his [[green card]]. Last month, their daughter Lina visited the [[consulate]], where the [[consul]] helped her. Lina told Anna about [[racism]] at her old school and a [[racist]] neighbor there. Before Kyiv, the family lived in a poor [[ghetto]] in a big, noisy city. Now her parents work hard and hope to join the [[middle class]] here. Anna's grandpa was born in the [[baby boom]], so he is a real [[baby boomer]]. He calls himself a [[nationalist]], so Lina asked him what that means. They had a long but friendly argument about [[nationalism]]. In the end, Grandpa smiled and said, "Every [[migrant]] is welcome at my table."

title: A day in parliament
scene: Anna's class visits parliament, and the secretariat gives them the agenda. A minister and the premier speak, the teacher explains that other countries have a senate with senators, a British Tory guest watches, a lobbyist from a big lobby waits in the hall, and the members try to reach a compromise and a consensus to keep the status quo and avoid a shutdown.

words.ex: The parliament will vote on the new law next week.
The new party has a clear political agenda.
Who is the new health minister?
The premier met with the president today.
Does your country have a senate?
I saw a senator on TV last night.
The lobbyist met with senators all week.
The oil lobby is very powerful in the capital.
We reached a compromise after a long talk.
The team finally reached a consensus on the plan.
Many people just want to keep the status quo.
The government shutdown lasted two weeks.
The minister held a press briefing this morning.
English is the de facto language of business.
The impeachment trial lasted three weeks.
I am going to a medical congress in May.
The congressman met with voters in our town.
The congresswoman visited our school last week.

old_story: On Thursday, Anna's class went on a school trip to [[parliament]]. A friendly guide explained that every party has its own political [[agenda]]. First, they watched a short press [[briefing]] in a bright hall. A young [[minister]] spoke about new schools, and then the [[premier]] talked about the budget. Mr. Koval explained that some countries have a [[senate]], where each [[senator]] votes on laws. In the hall, a [[lobbyist]] from the energy [[lobby]] waited with a thick folder. The members argued for hours but finally reached a [[compromise]]. The guide said full [[consensus]] is rare, because many people just want the [[status quo]]. Now they had a budget, so there would be no [[shutdown]] this year. Anna asked about [[impeachment]], and Mr. Koval explained it with a funny example. On the bus home, Max asked so many questions that he became the [[de facto]] guide.

title: Students protest
scene: Students protest against a new law. A young activist talks about activism, ideals, idealism and a utopia, a trade union joins the boycott, an anarchist shouts, a cynic calls the politicians hypocrites and their words nonsense, and a patriot talks about patriotism and liberalism.

words.ex: I went to a protest in the city center.
The activists marched to city hall.
Her activism helped change the law.
He is young and has very high ideals.
Young people are often full of idealism.
The writer described a perfect utopia.
He joined a trade union at the factory.
Students called for a boycott of the store.
An anarchist believes we do not need any government.
He is a cynic and doesn't trust anyone.
He tells us to save money, but he's a hypocrite.
That's complete nonsense!
Is there a train strike tomorrow?

old_story: On Saturday, Anna and Max joined a student [[protest]] near the university. The city wanted to close the student library and build a parking lot. A young [[activist]] named Sofia spoke first. She said her [[activism]] started in a small library like this one. "We have one [[ideal]]: free books for everyone," she said. Max liked her [[idealism]], but he did not believe in a perfect [[utopia]]. Then workers from a local [[trade union]] arrived with big signs. They called for a [[boycott]] of the new parking company. A man in a black hat said he was an [[anarchist]] and shouted at the sky. Max's friend Oleh, a real [[cynic]], called all the politicians [[hypocrites|hypocrite]]. He said the whole march was [[nonsense]]. Two weeks later, the city kept the library open, and even Oleh brought cake.

title: Anna's internship at a newspaper
scene: Anna works for a month in a newsroom. A journalist teaches her, a columnist writes an editorial, a correspondent calls from abroad with an exclusive about a scandal, a tabloid wants publicity, the publisher wants a rewrite of the morning digest, and the media wait for a briefing.

words.ex: The newsroom was busy before the evening show.
Are you a journalist?
She is a columnist for a local newspaper.
The newspaper's editorial criticized the new city plan.
She is a foreign correspondent in Paris.
The magazine got an exclusive with the actor.
Did you hear about the scandal at the school?
The tabloid printed rumors about the singer.
The scandal brought the company a lot of bad publicity.
The game's publisher announced a new release date.
The article needs a rewrite before we publish it.
I read the news on social media.
The government pushed a different narrative.
The mass media cover the election every day.
I read the morning news digest on my phone.
I want to be a TV reporter.
The company hired a firm to handle PR.

old_story: In July, Anna started a month-long internship in a busy [[newsroom]]. An older [[journalist]] named Petro showed her how to check every fact. Next to him sat a [[columnist]] who was writing the Sunday [[editorial]]. At noon, a [[correspondent]] called from abroad with an [[exclusive]]. She had proof of a big [[scandal]] at a local football club. A [[tabloid]] already had rumors about it. "They want [[publicity]], not facts," Petro said. The [[publisher]] read the morning [[digest]] and asked for a quick [[rewrite]]. He wanted the true story, not the old [[narrative]] about the club. By evening, all the [[media]] were waiting outside the club for a briefing. Petro let Anna write the headline. The next morning, the [[mass media]] everywhere repeated it.

title: Anna's cousin in the army
scene: Anna's cousin was a cadet; now he is an officer and trains new recruits. He tells her about his lieutenant and his sergeant, his battalion and a convoy at a checkpoint, a bunker, camouflage, drones, a tank and a sniper, and about the victory parade they all dream of.

words.ex: The young cadet saluted the officer.
I want to be an army officer.
The new recruits arrived at the army base today.
Where is the lieutenant?
Is the sergeant here today?
The battalion moved to the front line at night.
A convoy of trucks brought food to the city.
We stopped at a police checkpoint.
Soldiers hid in the bunker during the attack.
The soldiers wore camouflage in the forest.
He flies a drone in the park.
A tank moved slowly across the field.
What time does the parade start tomorrow?
He is a true patriot and loves his country.
Both combatants agreed to stop fighting.
The adjutant gave the general's orders to the troops.
My grandfather was an admiral in the navy.
The commodore gave orders to the fleet.
The commandant of the base gave new orders.

old_story: Anna's cousin Taras was a [[cadet]] only four years ago. Now he is an [[officer]], and he trains every new [[recruit]]. On Sunday, he visited Anna and told stories over tea. His [[lieutenant]] is strict but fair, and his [[sergeant]] tells terrible jokes. Last month, his [[battalion]] practiced moving a [[convoy]] of trucks through a [[checkpoint]]. They slept one night in a cold [[bunker]] and wore [[camouflage]] in the forest. A small [[drone]] watched them from above, and a [[tank]] moved slowly behind. In the exercise, half of the soldiers played enemy [[combatants|combatant]]. Taras was the colonel's [[adjutant]], so he carried the orders on foot. Anna asked why he chose the army. "I'm a [[patriot]], and I want my family safe," he said. Most of all, they all dream of marching in a big peace [[parade]] together.
